page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARM64 architecture using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 core design, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the c6gn.xlarge demonstrates average performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, placing it in the middle 50% of tested servers. Large-block memory bandwidth for both read and write operations also performs at an average level, alongside Passmark database operations. However, the instance exhibits weaker performance in Geekbench suites, Passmark CPU tests, and single-threaded compression tasks. Large-model operations and LLM inference tasks show poor performance, reflecting the lack of specialized vector or matrix extensions like AVX-512 or AMX.

The qualitative cost efficiency of this instance is tied to its ARM64 architecture, which typically offers a lower resource-to-compute cost ratio compared to traditional x86 architectures for compatible software stacks. Because it lacks local SSD storage and GPU accelerators, it is best utilized for network-optimized workloads, distributed database nodes, containerized microservices, and general ARM-native compute tasks that rely on network-attached storage.
